title: The AI Debate Gets More Complicated: Microsoft Has a Win, Meta Stumbles | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman abandons his Charter recommendation after worsening broadband losses. He separates hyperscaler infrastructure moats from vulnerable model-provider economics, warns about customer concentration and price competition, and favors selective AI beneficiaries. The earnings discussion contrasts cloud growth with capital intensity and revisits FICO, Meritage, payment companies and portfolio risk.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Reject thesis creep when the original operating premise fails.
Distinguish infrastructure barriers from model-level switching costs.
Evaluate cash flow and hidden capital commitments alongside earnings growth.
Portfolio risk management matters independently of subject expertise.
tools_and_charts: AI share drawdowns and CoreWeave borrowing yield
Corporate EPS, revenue, capex and free cash flow
Historical world GDP per capita chart attributed to John Cassidy
transcript_cautions: The transcript calls the SOX index an iShares ETF, mixing an index and fund identifier.
Microsoft EPS growth mixes a $4.74 adjusted figure with a different growth comparison.
The historical GDP graph is an aggregate; it cannot establish that every individual became wealthier.

claims.claim: The Charter recovery thesis has failed for now: broadband losses worsened for two successive quarters, reaching 172,000 in Q2, so cheap valuation alone no longer justifies holding.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the stated proposition with Charter second-quarter 2026 earnings. Preserve the metric, reporting period and conditions; agreement on direction alone does not prove a causal explanation.
claims.reason: Charter confirms the Q2 subscriber loss and weakening operating results. Abandoning the valuation thesis is a portfolio judgment, not an independently correct future-return forecast.

evidence.title: Charter second-quarter 2026 earnings
evidence.finding: Internet customers declined 172,000 versus 116,000 in 2Q25; revenue down 1.7%, adjusted EBITDA down 4.3%; debt repurchases $1.2bn principal.
